metadata.name: CI/CD Pipeline & Cloud Manifest Templates
metadata.description: Six copy-ready CI/CD and deployment templates (GitHub Actions CI, GitHub Actions container publishing, GitLab CI, Docker Compose, Kubernetes and AWS ECS Fargate), each stored as JSON and as ready-to-paste YAML or JSON, validated with each platform's own tooling and hardened with current security defaults.

github_actions_node_ci.description: Node.js test workflow across the two supported LTS lines (22 and 24) with npm caching, concurrency cancellation and a read-only token.
github_actions_node_ci.use_when: You need CI for a Node.js repository on GitHub.
security_highlights: Workflow token limited to contents: read.
Third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs (version noted in a comment).
persist-credentials: false keeps the token out of the checked-out .git folder.
timeout-minutes stops hung jobs from using runner minutes.
github_actions_node_ci.yaml:
name: CI
'on':
  push:
    branches:
    - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
    - main
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node-version:
        - 22.x
        - 24.x
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Set up Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        cache: npm
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci
    - name: Test
      run: npm test

github_actions_docker_ghcr.description: Builds a container image with Buildx and pushes it to GitHub Container Registry with branch, semver and SHA tags, build cache, SBOM and provenance attestations.
github_actions_docker_ghcr.use_when: You publish a Docker image from a GitHub repository.
security_highlights: Workflow default is contents: read; only the publish job gets packages: write.
Authenticates with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, no long-lived registry password.
Generates an SBOM and max-mode provenance attestation with the image.
Actions pinned to full commit SHAs.
customize: Branch and tag patterns under on:

steps.name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry

github_actions_docker_ghcr.yaml:
name: Publish container image
'on':
  push:
    branches:
    - main
    tags:
    - v*.*.*
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1
    - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    - name: Generate image tags
      id: meta
      uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
      with:
        images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
        tags: |-
          type=ref,event=branch
          type=semver,pattern={{version}}
          type=sha
    - name: Build and push
      uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
        labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
        cache-from: type=gha
        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
        provenance: mode=max
        sbom: true

gitlab_ci_multi_stage.description: Lint, test, build and deploy pipeline with GitLab SAST, npm caching keyed on the lockfile, JUnit reports, Docker-in-Docker image builds and a manual production deploy.
gitlab_ci_multi_stage.use_when: You build and ship a Node.js service on GitLab.
security_highlights: GitLab SAST template included (runs in the test stage).
Registry login uses --password-stdin, so the password never appears in the process list.
Production deploy is manual, limited to the default branch and serialized with resource_group.
Pipelines run only for merge requests and the default branch (workflow rules).

script: echo "Deploy $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHA with your release tool here"

gitlab_ci_multi_stage.yaml:
include:
- template: Jobs/SAST.gitlab-ci.yml
stages:
- lint
- test
- build
- deploy
workflow:
  rules:
  - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == 'merge_request_event'
  - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
default:
  image: node:24-alpine
  interruptible: true
  cache:
    key:
      files:
      - package-lock.json
    paths:
    - .npm/
  before_script:
  - npm ci --cache .npm --prefer-offline
lint:
  stage: lint
  script:
  - npm run lint
unit_tests:
  stage: test
  script:
  - npm test
  artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
      junit: junit.xml
    expire_in: 7 days
build_image:
  stage: build
  image: docker:29
  services:
  - docker:29-dind
  variables:
    DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: /certs
  cache: []
  before_script:
  - echo "$CI_REGISTRY_PASSWORD" | docker login "$CI_REGISTRY" -u "$CI_REGISTRY_USER" --password-stdin
  script:
  - docker build -t "$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHA" .
  - docker push "$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHA"
  rules:
  - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
deploy_production:
  stage: deploy
  image: alpine:3.24
  cache: []
  before_script: []
  script:
  - echo "Deploy $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHA with your release tool here"
  environment:
    name: production
    url: https://app.example.com
  resource_group: production
  interruptible: false
  rules:
  - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
    when: manual

docker_compose_production.description: Web API, PostgreSQL 18 and Redis 8 with health-gated startup, Docker secrets, an internal-only backend network and persistent volumes.
docker_compose_production.use_when: You run a small production or staging stack on a single host.
security_highlights: API runs as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges.
Database password delivered as a Docker secret file, never as a plain environment variable.
Database and cache sit on an internal network with no outside access.
API port bound to 127.0.0.1 so it is only reachable through a reverse proxy on the host.
docker_compose_production.yaml:
name: app
services:
  web:
    image: registry.example.com/app:1.2.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: 10001:10001
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
    - /tmp
    security_opt:
    - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
    - ALL
    ports:
    - 127.0.0.1:8080:8080
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      DATABASE_HOST: db
      DATABASE_NAME: app_prod
      DATABASE_USER: app_user
      DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/db_password
      REDIS_URL: redis://cache:6379
    secrets:
    - db_password
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      cache:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '1.5'
          memory: 1024M
    networks:
    - frontend
    - backend
  db:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: app_prod
      POSTGRES_USER: app_user
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/db_password
    secrets:
    - db_password
    volumes:
    - db_data:/var/lib/postgresql
    healthcheck:
      test:
      - CMD-SHELL
      - pg_isready -U app_user -d app_prod
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 20s
    networks:
    - backend
  cache:
    image: redis:8-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
    - redis-server
    - --appendonly
    - 'yes'
    volumes:
    - cache_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test:
      - CMD
      - redis-cli
      - ping
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
    networks:
    - backend
networks:
  frontend: {}
  backend:
    internal: true
volumes:
  db_data: {}
  cache_data: {}
secrets:
  db_password:
    file: ./secrets/db_password.txt

kubernetes_zero_downtime.description: Deployment, Service, PodDisruptionBudget and HorizontalPodAutoscaler for a stateless HTTP API, meeting the Pod Security Standards restricted profile.
kubernetes_zero_downtime.use_when: You deploy a stateless web service to Kubernetes 1.33 or newer.
security_highlights: Meets the restricted Pod Security Standard: non-root, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, RuntimeDefault seccomp.
Read-only root filesystem with a size-limited emptyDir for /tmp.
Service account token not mounted (the API does not call the Kubernetes API).
Zero downtime: maxUnavailable 0, readiness probe, preStop sleep for endpoint removal and a PodDisruptionBudget for node drains.
kubernetes_zero_downtime.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: example-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: api
      app.kubernetes.io/part-of: example-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: api
        app.kubernetes.io/part-of: example-app
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        fsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: registry.example.com/app:1.2.0
        ports:
        - name: http
          containerPort: 8080
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - ALL
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          limits:
            memory: 512Mi
        startupProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: http
          periodSeconds: 5
          failureThreshold: 24
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /readyz
            port: http
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: http
          periodSeconds: 20
          failureThreshold: 3
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            sleep:
              seconds: 5
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tmp
          mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
      - name: tmp
        emptyDir:
          sizeLimit: 64Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: example-app
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: example-app
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: http
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: example-app
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: api
      app.kubernetes.io/part-of: example-app
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: api
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: example-app
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: api
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70

aws_ecs_fargate_task.description: Fargate task definition with separate execution and task roles, a single key pulled from AWS Secrets Manager, CloudWatch Logs and a read-only root filesystem.
aws_ecs_fargate_task.use_when: You run a container service on ECS Fargate.
security_highlights: Execution role (image pull, secrets, logs) separated from the task role used by your code.
Pulls one JSON key from Secrets Manager instead of the whole secret.
Runs as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem and a writable /tmp volume.
Image pinned to a version tag instead of latest.
customize: Account ID, region and role names
